cues.en: But our goal is to build interactive apps without JavaScript or without writing JavaScript and the goal isn't just how can we not write JavaScript? cues.zh: 但我们的目标是构建无需 JavaScript、或者无需编写 JavaScript 的交互式应用。目标并不只是“我们怎样才能不写 JavaScript？”而是“我们怎样才能真正提出一个合理的编程模型？”比如，怎样在服务端写 Elixir，最后还能做出非常有吸引力的东西？所以用 Live View，我们有一个极其简单的编程模型。如果你是 Elixir 新手，几乎马上就能理解它，而且它可不是玩具。

cues.en: So it's highly optimized for not only building apps quickly, but also building them with incredible performance. So when people originally hear this idea of server-rendered real-time apps, they're doubtful and they'll think it's going to be too heavy or too slow. cues.zh: 因此，它经过了高度优化，不仅能快速构建应用，还能带来令人难以置信的优异性能。很多人刚听到“服务端渲染的实时应用”这个概念时都会持怀疑态度，觉得它肯定太重或太慢了。台下可能也有很多人还在犹豫观望，但我希望在今天的演讲中能够说服大家。

cues.en: But what we're able to do is have a super simple programming model doing something that's seemingly very heavy resource-wise on the server and on the client, but actually do it in a way that's really compelling and really fast. cues.zh: 但我们能做到的是：用一个超简单的编程模型，去做在服务器和客户端上看起来资源开销极大的事情，而且实际上做得既惊艳又飞快。接下来我们会深入 Live View 内部，看看在演讲剩余部分如何实现这一点。Live View 公开大概两三周了，人们已经做出了一些相当亮眼的成果。所以我想展示其中几个。Live View 已经公开可用，但还没上 Hex。

cues.en: We take on a lot of the client side single page apps app complexity out of good business reasons, but we end up adopting a lot more complexity than we had originally planned. cues.zh: 出于合理的业务原因，我们承担了客户端单页应用的大量复杂性，但最终却引入了比原计划多得多的复杂性。因为我觉得，如果我们真的扪心自问，至少我作为顾问，在多个不同领域做过几十个应用的经验是这样。

cues.en: I've never had a single app that actually justified a full client side application solution, right? Like I've never had to write Google docs in the browser. Uh, if I had to, I would absolutely reach for a client side framework, but there's always been just parts of the app that have needed this kind of rich interactive experience. So I think a lot of us are using single page app frameworks for good reasons because we need those bits of interaction. And usually if we have to go in, if we have to go all in and buy into a framework because we need to accomplish these interactive
cues.zh: 我做过的应用里，没有哪个真的需要纯客户端应用的方案，对吧？比如我从没在浏览器里写过 Google Docs。额，如果非写不可，我肯定会选客户端框架，但其实往往只是应用的某些部分需要这种富交互体验。所以我认为我们很多人用单页应用框架是有正当理由的，因为我们需要那些交互功能。通常如果我们必须全力投入，必须全盘接受某个框架来搞定这些交互

cues.en: business requirements, then we have, we have no choice but to buy into the complexity. But I think ultimately we fall on the spectrum of like, we don't need all that complexity for the entirety of our application, but we, if we have to buy in any way, we have to train our team. If we already have to send Ember JS down to client or send React down to the client, then why aren't we writing the rest of the app in React? So I think a lot of people are, are adopting single page apps when they really don't need them for the majority of the application. If only they had an alternative.
cues.zh: 业务需求，那我们就不得不接受其带来的复杂性。但我认为归根结底，我们在这种权衡中会发现，整个应用其实并不需要那么多复杂性，可要是横竖都得接受，就得培训团队；既然反正都要把 Ember JS 或 React 打包推给客户端，那为什么不顺手把剩下的部分也全用 React 写了呢？所以我认为很多人都在盲目采用单页应用，即使整个应用的大部分场景根本不需要。要是他们能有别的选择就好了。

cues.en: And that's where I think things live view is going to be one alternative to allow you to defer or avoid this massive rabbit hole of complexity that is client side development because it is super complex. I think, you know, I've been doing web development for my entire programming career. cues.zh: 而我认为，这正是像 LiveView 这类方案能成为一种替代选择的地方：它可以让你推迟或避开客户端开发这个巨大的复杂性无底洞，因为客户端开发实在太复杂了。你知道，我整个编程生涯都在做 Web 开发。我觉得我们很多日常做 Web 开发的人，多少会忘记现代 Web——或者说整个 Web——到底存在多少层复杂性。对吧。所以

cues.en: Like the whole request response lifecycle. That's an entire mental model and understanding that you internalize and you don't think about. So let's just walk through one example. So if we're trying to render this beautiful thermostat here, it's ultimately a glorified counter. But let's just say let's do something simple. We want to render this thermostat.
cues.zh: 比如整个请求-响应生命周期。那是你早已内化、甚至不用去想的整套心智模型和理解。但无论是初学者还是资深程序员，想要在网页上实现某些效果，背后其实涉及大量的层级、决策和思考过程。那我们就来看一个例子。假设我们想渲染出这里漂亮的恒温器，它说白了就是一个高级点的计数器。但我们先做点简单的，我们想渲染这个恒温器。

cues.en: which is ultimately just showing integer value and allowing the user to update, decrement or increment that value. When we start out writing it, you know, our designer will give us some CSS and we end up having a static web page with this beautiful thermostat and like we're feeling good. Like this is super simple to whip up. But the moment we want to make this interactive, like we suddenly have to start bringing on complexity, making decisions. cues.en: But then the decisions like have to start being made. Like what does the server side look like? Like you said define the routes, right? Like a thermostat controller or thermostat channel. I have to write that code. I have to define the payload contracts.

cues.en: Here, I'm inlining some EX, but you could have a separate EX file if you wanted to. And when we mount a live view, we assign some initial state. We call render, and we're done. cues.zh: 在这里，我内联了一些 EX 代码，但如果你愿意，也可以单独放在一个 EX 文件里。挂载 LiveView 时，我们会分配一些初始状态。然后调用 render，就完成了。但现在，由于 LiveView 是有状态的，每当触发像点击按钮增减这样的事件时，我们就会改变状态，这就是 LiveView 和 React 的工作机制。大部分这种响应式编程框架，都是只要遇到状态改变，就会调用 render。

cues.en: And we update the UI with the updated HTML. So Phoenix Live, you kind of just like abstracts the fact that that happens to go over the network. But the programming model is very straightforward, right? It's like we have this cycle of we've got a render function that produces HTML. Any time we experience a state change, we call render. That produces new HTML. The browser's updated. And then we wait for events. And we can annotate the client with like PHX click.
cues.zh: 然后我们用更新后的 HTML 来更新 UI。所以 Phoenix LiveView 基本上抽象掉了“这其实是通过网络传输的”这一事实。但它的编程模型非常直观，对吧？它就像一个循环：我们有一个生成 HTML 的 render 函数，每当状态发生改变，我们就调用 render，生成新的 HTML，浏览器随之更新，然后我们等待事件发生。我们还可以在客户端使用类似 phx-click 的属性来进行标注。

cues.en: we can annotate forms with like anytime a form event's changed or submitted, we can do PHX submit. That gets sent to the server and your server callback is run. If you don't change your state, nothing happens. If you do change your state, render gets called and we update the UI. So it's this very simple cycle. And this is almost the entirety of the programming model, except for the fact that we have a stateful system. So we've seen other, other languages have seen like
cues.zh: 我们可以给表单加上注解，比如每当表单事件发生改变或提交时，就能触发 phx-submit，将其发送给服务器并执行你的服务器端回调；如果你没有改变状态，就什么都不会发生；而如果你改变了状态，render 就会被调用，进而更新 UI。所以这就是一个非常简单的循环，并且这几乎就是该编程模型的全部，除了我们拥有一个有状态系统这一事实。因此我们看到其他语言也注意到了

cues.en: what we're doing with live view and have been inspired by it. You can set a post request to the server, send all the state to the server, re-render the server, re-render the HTML and you.
cues.zh: 我们在 LiveView 上做的事情，也受到了它的启发。现在 Ruby 和 PHP 里也有类似项目，是受 LiveView 启发的，这很棒。但我觉得大多数人忽略的是，我们有一个有状态平台可以基于它来构建。所以你可以想象，这里可以是一个有状态进程。抱歉，是一个有状态循环，客户端持有所有状态。你可以向服务器发一个 POST 请求，把所有状态发给服务器，让服务器重新渲染，重新渲染 HTML，然后你……

cues.en: you could simulate an interactive experience, but there would be no process running on the server. So it would work for our counter example, but it wouldn't work for something where you want to actually push updates down to the browser. And worse, you'd have to send all this HTML on the wire and all the state for every state change. Because if we want to suddenly become a stateful system, this is where like it looks, it really shines. Like we actually have a platform that can start a process that's cheap and actually react to events that are happening. And for me, this is like, this is our secret sauce. It's not something that the live you team did. It's the fact that we can,
cues.zh: 你可以模拟出交互体验，但服务器上并没有运行任何进程。所以对于我们这个计数器例子是可行的，但如果你想真正把更新推送到浏览器，它就行不通了。更糟糕的是，每次状态改变，你都得在网络上传输所有这些 HTML 和全部状态。因为如果我们想突然变成一个有状态的系统，这正是它大放异彩的地方。比如我们确实拥有一个可以低成本启动进程、并对发生的事件做出实际响应的平台。对我来说，这就是我们的制胜秘诀。这并不是 LiveView 团队做了什么，而是因为我们能够——

cues.en: like Elixir was built for stateful systems. So this is cheap for us to do. Like in other platforms, this is going to be incredibly expensive, but for us, it's actually viable. And again, the model is anytime I experience a state change. So in this case, I have a handle info tick callback.
cues.zh: 毕竟 Elixir 本身就是为有状态系统而构建的。所以这对我们来说成本很低。如果在其他平台上，这么做会极其昂贵，但对我们来说却是完全可行的。因为假设你想给温控器加个定时器，它就会在服务器端按秒计时，而我们会把更新实时推送到客户端。我们总不能让客户端每秒都轮询一次服务器，对吧？所以在这种情况下，我们只需在挂载且连接成功时，每秒给自己发一条消息就行了。再说一次，这种模型就是：任何时候只要我经历了状态变化——比如这里，我就有一个 handle_info 的 tick 回调函数。

cues.en: Because, ultimately, live user-generated servers, if I assign a new time on every second tick, my state changes, render gets called, and I update the UI. And I can do this because I have a stateful process running on the server. You can't simulate this over stateless HTTP. So this is kind of utilizing what's there in the platform to do this efficiently, even though it still seems crazy. But I think as we go further and further today, hopefully I will dispel any myths about this being a non-viable solution.
cues.zh: 因为归根结底，在实时的用户生成服务器上，如果我每一秒都赋一个新时间，状态就会改变，render 就会被调用，UI 也会随之更新。而我能做到这一点，是因为服务器上运行着一个有状态的进程。这在无状态的 HTTP 上是无法模拟的。所以这算是在利用平台现有的特性来高效实现这一点，尽管它听起来依然很疯狂。但我相信随着今天的深入讲解，希望我能消除大家认为这种方案不可行的迷思。

So like the programming models, super simple,
cues.zh: 因为进程很便宜，而且这个平台就是为大规模处理进程而构建的。我们已经用 200 万个网站连接证明了这一点，归根结底，LiveView 构建在 Phoenix channels 之上。所以我们知道 Phoenix channels 能处理数百万连接，而最终 LiveView 只是一个 Phoenix channel 进程。因此，我们构建在平台和框架的原语之上，让这些事情发生。这样每秒我们都能更新状态、对 UI 做增量更新，但还不止这些。比如编程模型，超级简单，

cues.en: from inception to death of a live view. And it turns out there's like a perfect emoji lifecycle for Phoenix, which is quite pleasing. So live view starts in your router with a live macro. So you can just say like, hey, if there's a get request to slash thermostat, I can route directly to a live view. So the controller layer,
cues.zh: 从 LiveView 的诞生到消亡。事实证明，Phoenix 有一套非常完美的 Emoji 生命周期，这很讨喜。所以我们要逐步梳理一下 LiveView 是如何启动的、页面在真正连接到服务器时会发生什么，以及当这些东西崩溃时又会发生什么。LiveView 是从路由里的 live 宏开始的。所以你只需写上：嘿，如果有一个指向 /thermostat 的 GET 请求，我就可以直接路由到一个 LiveView。这样控制器层

So I could write live slash thermostat my router and then I write a render function and a malfunction.
cues.zh: 呃，就完全不需要了。所以就像我之前说的，请求-响应这整套概念都不复存在了。因此，当你在 Elixir，抱歉，是在 Phoenix 中编写 LiveView 时，控制器层在 LiveView 的生命周期中基本没什么戏份。因为它的唯一任务就是把页面最初渲染出来，之后就由 LiveView 接管了。所以我可以在路由里写 live "/thermostat"，然后写一个 render 函数和一个 mount 函数。

cues.en: And in this case, you can pass some session information that's tamper-proof and signed. So if I want to get the current user out of the session, I can't rely on the plug necessarily. cues.zh: 在这种情况下，你可以传递一些防篡改且已签名的会话信息。所以如果我想从会话中获取当前用户，不一定能依赖 plug。但我可以对该数据签名，然后在挂载时获取用户。而且在挂载时，你可能会从系统获取某些恒温器的读数。你给 socket 赋值，我们进行渲染，就搞定了。

cues.en: But there's a key step in this lifecycle where the first time we call render, we just send static HTML down and we don't spawn any processes. Because our goal is like we don't want to be like a single page app where like we render the, we don't render the shell of an application and then send no HTML down. Like when you call, like I could curl slash thermostat and I'm gonna get the HTML to the thermostat. It's because static HTML and no processes respond. So your, the initial request is stateless. And then we reattach later.
cues.zh: 但这个生命周期里有个关键步骤：第一次调用 render 时，我们只下发静态 HTML，不启动任何进程。因为我们的目标是不想做成单页应用那样——只渲染应用外壳，却不下发任何 HTML。比如你可以调用，比如我可以 curl /thermostat，就能拿到恒温器的 HTML。这是因为有静态 HTML，而且没有进程来响应。所以初始请求是无状态的。之后我们再重新挂接。

cues.en: So step one is we have a get request of thermostat. We call your thermostat live mount. You do some assigns. You fetch from the database. You do what you need to do. Render gets called. We produce HTML, and we send a 200 HTML response. And we're done. So if you never navigated or if you have JavaScript disabled, you're going to get that beautiful thermostat. It's not going to do anything, but you get the HTML. So like SEO just works.
cues.zh: 第一步，我们收到对温控器的 GET 请求，调用你的温控器 LiveView 的 mount，你做一些赋值，从数据库拉取数据，做你想做的事情，调用 render，生成 HTML，然后返回一个 200 HTML 响应，这就搞定了；所以即便你从不跳转，或者禁用了 JavaScript，也能看到那个漂亮的温控器，虽然它不能交互，但你能拿到 HTML，所以 SEO 就天然支持了，

cues.en: you don't have to worry about it. Uh, you're protected from like denial of service attacks, right? So like if someone tried to throw, uh, like with work or Apache bench, like a ton of requests at this app, you wouldn't be spawning a hundred thousand library requests per second. They'd actually literally have to, uh, start like a headless, uh, headless browser instance and really connect because the second step of this process is once we've rendered, we've done the data fetching, the browser is going to reconnect over web sockets using Phoenix channels.
cues.zh: 你完全不用操心。而且你还能防御拒绝服务攻击，对吧？比如有人用 wrk 或 ApacheBench 向这个应用狂发海量请求，你并不会每秒生成十万个 LiveView 请求，他们实际上必须去启动无头浏览器实例才能真正连接上，因为这个流程的第二步是：一旦渲染完成、取完数据，浏览器就会利用 Phoenix channels 通过 WebSocket 重新连接。

cues.en: Then we're going to start a process. So we've signed some data down. So we know when you connect whether or not this was actually a valid initial render. So there's no way that someone can just reconnect with a user ID and fake a current user. Like there's the data that we put in the session was signed. So we connect, we started a process, then we call your mount. So there's this two step, there's this two step process. So mount gets called again. If we have to fetch current user, we'll fetch it again. So in your logs, you may see for a given web request,
cues.zh: 然后我们会启动一个流程。所以我们已经把一些数据签名后下发。这样你连接时，我们就知道这次是否真的是有效的初始渲染。因此，别人没法只靠一个用户 ID 重连并伪造当前用户。比如，我们放进 session 的数据是签过名的。于是我们连接、启动流程，然后调用你的 mount。所以有这么两步，是个两步流程。因此 mount 会被再次调用。如果我们需要获取当前用户，就会再取一次。所以在日志里，你可能会看到对于某个 Web 请求，

cues.en: two database fetches. That's because we did the static request response and then we have to do this second initial stateful mount. Then we call render and we send HTML back. But now we have a process spawned. So now we enter this second cycle of just waiting for state changes to happen. And whether that's a message arriving on the server in a handle info callback and changing our state or whether that's a client clicking a plus or minus button, whatever happens on the server, a state change is invoked.
cues.zh: 两次数据库查询。这是因为我们先执行了静态的“请求-响应”，随后又必须执行这第二次初始的有状态 mount。然后我们调用 render 并返回 HTML。但现在我们已经生成了一个进程。于是我们进入了这第二个周期，专门等待状态改变的发生。无论是服务器收到一条消息并在 handle info 回调中改变了我们的状态，还是客户端点击了加号或减号按钮，只要服务器上发生任何事，都会触发状态改变。

cues.en: if it changes your state, we call render and the UI is going to be updated. So there's this two-step process that is almost hidden from you because it's the same code path, whether you're coming over an initial HTTP request or you're being mounted a second time. And this may seem like a odd limitation, but we went through like we want it to be, we want to be protected from denial of service. We want to be, uh, we just want to return HTML initially, but we also have to have a code path that let's say like you drop connection. So if I'm looking at my thermostat,
cues.zh: 如果它改变了你的状态，我们就会调用 render，界面就会更新。所以这个两步过程对你来说几乎是无感的，因为无论你是通过初始 HTTP 请求进入，还是第二次挂载，走的都是同一条代码路径。这看起来可能像个奇怪的限制，但我们之前考虑过，比如我们希望能够防范拒绝服务攻击。我们希望……呃，我们一开始只想返回 HTML，但我们也必须保留一条代码路径来应对掉线等情况。所以如果我正在看温控器，

cues.en: and then my connection drops, I have to be able to reconnect without a full page refresh. In order to do that, I need a code path that has all my necessary minimal data that can go call mount and go through the same setup. So it turns out that this programming model, even though you have to do maybe some little bit of extra data fetching, it allows you to do the initial HTTP requests, the initial website connection, and error recovery, all in the same code path. So we're able to do three things in one code path, and you ultimately don't have to think
cues.zh: 然后我的连接断开了，我必须能够在不刷新整个页面的情况下重新连接。为了做到这一点，我需要一条包含所有必要最小数据的代码路径，以便调用 mount 并走相同的初始化流程。事实证明，这种编程模型虽然可能需要多抓取一点点数据，但它能让你在同一条代码路径中处理初始 HTTP 请求、初始网站连接以及错误恢复。所以我们能用一条代码路径搞定三件事，你最终完全不必操心

cues.en: about like, okay, now what do I do if this website connection drops? It's like, no, it's all built in. It just calls mount again when you reconnect and everything recovers. And I think, I mentioned like we don't have our secret sauce, but I think one thing that you could say is our secret sauce is a live ex optimizations. So apart from what like just the VM gives us as far as scalable, cheap processes, we were able to really optimize since it looks kind of the whole approach of getting data down to the client and having that actually work efficiently.
cues.zh: 类似“好吧，如果网站连接断了，我现在该怎么办？”这种问题。不用管，它完全是内置的。重连时它只会再次调用 mount，所有东西就都恢复了。我想……我之前提过我们没有什么独门秘诀，但我觉得硬要说有什么秘诀的话，那就是 LiveView 的优化。因此，除了 VM 为我们提供的可扩展、轻量级进程之外，我们还能够真正优化——毕竟它涵盖了将数据下发到客户端并使其高效运作的整套方案。
